name: finance-toolkit
description: Give AI assistants access to 500+ financial methods calculated transparently from raw financial statements, not pulled from third-party endpoints.
long_description:
The Finance Toolkit gives AI assistants access to 500+ financial methods calculated transparently from raw financial statements. This includes financial statements, historical prices, analyst estimates, 100+ fundamental ratios, 55+ technical indicators, 85+ risk and performance metrics, 45+ econometric tests and estimators, and 90+ macro and fixed income indicators.

A Financial Modeling Prep API key is required to access 30+ years of financial data. Obtain one at [jeroenbouma.com/fmp](https://jeroenbouma.com/fmp). Authenticate once via OAuth, no key is stored on the server. Rate limit fallback to Yahoo Finance is built in, and macro databases from OECD and GMDB are accessed independently.

tools.name: efficiency
tools.description: Pre-computed efficiency ratios (asset turnover, inventory turnover, days sales outstanding, days payable outstanding, cash conversion cycle). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Use instead of raw financial statements. Supports quarterly=true and start_date/end_date.

tools.name: liquidity
tools.description: Pre-computed liquidity ratios (current ratio, quick ratio, cash ratio, working capital). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Use instead of raw financial statements. Supports quarterly=true and start_date/end_date.

tools.name: profitability
tools.description: Pre-computed profitability ratios (gross margin, operating margin, net margin, ROE, ROA, ROIC, ROCE). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Use instead of raw financial statements. Supports quarterly=true and start_date/end_date.

tools.name: solvency
tools.description: Pre-computed solvency ratios (debt-to-equity, interest coverage, debt-to-assets, net debt to EBITDA). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Use instead of raw financial statements. Supports quarterly=true and start_date/end_date.

tools.name: valuation
tools.description: Pre-computed valuation ratios (P/E, EPS, EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT, P/B, P/S, PEG, dividend yield, FCF yield, market cap, forward P/E, forward PEG). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Use instead of raw financial statements. Supports quarterly=true and start_date/end_date. get_forward_price_earnings_ratio and get_forward_price_earnings_growth_ratio additionally require a Premium FMP subscription and are fetched on first use only.

tools.name: breadth
tools.description: Market breadth technical indicators (McClellan Oscillator, OBV, Advance/Decline Line, Chaikin, TRIN, new highs and lows). Applied to price data automatically — no need to fetch prices first. TRIN treats the given tickers as one market, so every column holds the same value; pass the market's constituents for a meaningful figure. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers.

tools.name: momentum
tools.description: Momentum technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Stochastic Oscillator, Williams %R, Aroon, ADX, CCI, MFI, rate of change, Ichimoku Cloud, awesome, ultimate and Chande momentum oscillators, vortex, Know Sure Thing and more). Applied to price data automatically — no need to fetch prices first. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers.

tools.name: overlap
tools.description: Overlap technical indicators drawn over the price (simple, exponential, double exponential, triangular, weighted, Hull and Kaufman adaptive moving averages, TRIX, VWAP, Parabolic SAR, pivot points, Fibonacci retracement levels, support and resistance levels). Applied to price data automatically — no need to fetch prices first. Bollinger Bands and Keltner Channels are in the volatility tool. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers.

tools.name: volatility
tools.description: Volatility technical indicators (Bollinger Bands, Keltner Channels, Donchian Channels, True Range, Average True Range, Supertrend, volatility cone). Applied to price data automatically — no need to fetch prices first. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers.

tools.name: models
tools.description: Pre-computed financial models (WACC, DuPont analysis, Extended DuPont analysis, Enterprise value breakdown, intrinsic value/DCF, Gordon Growth Model, Altman Z-Score, Piotroski F-Score, Beneish M-Score, Economic Value Added (EVA), Present Value of Growth Opportunities, Sustainable Growth Rate, Internal Growth Rate, Graham Number). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Supports quarterly=true and start_date/end_date.

tools.name: performance
tools.description: Pre-computed risk-adjusted performance metrics (Sharpe ratio incl. standard/adjusted/probabilistic/deflated methods, Sortino ratio, Alpha, Jensen's Alpha, Beta, CAPM, Treynor ratio, M2 ratio, Tracking Error, Information Ratio, Fama-French factors, period Returns, Excess Returns — Returns/Excess Returns support cumulative=true for a compounded growth index rebased to 1). Beta, CAPM, Alpha, Jensen's Alpha, Treynor, Sortino, M2, Tracking Error and Information Ratio support rolling=N for a rolling N-period value spanning the full history instead of one value per period (e.g. period='monthly', rolling=6 for a rolling 6-month figure). Sharpe ratios are per observation (e.g. per day within the period) unless annualize=true. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Supports period='daily' only together with rolling=N (e.g. period='daily', rolling=60 for a rolling 60-day figure); per-period results use weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly.

tools.name: risk
tools.description: Pre-computed risk metrics (VaR incl. historic/gaussian/cf/studentt/evt distributions, CVaR, EVaR, GARCH volatility, max drawdown, drawdown duration, drawdown recovery time, Conditional Drawdown at Risk (CDaR), Tail Ratio, skewness, kurtosis, downside deviation, Variance, Volatility incl. close_to_close/parkinson/garman_klass/rogers_satchell/yang_zhang estimators, Excess Volatility). VaR, CVaR, skewness, kurtosis, CDaR, Tail Ratio, downside deviation, Variance, Volatility and Excess Volatility support rolling=N for a rolling N-period value spanning the full history instead of one value per period (e.g. period='monthly', rolling=6 for a rolling 6-month figure). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. Supports period='daily' for whole-series calculations; rolling and per-period outputs use weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly. get_copula_simulation returns 100 simulated joint draws unless n_simulations= asks for more. get_amihud_illiquidity is the price impact per billion dollars traded (scale=1e9).

tools.name: econometrics
tools.description: Statistical and econometric analysis of price or return series: unit root tests (ADF, KPSS, Phillips-Perron, Zivot-Andrews), cointegration (Engle-Granger, Johansen, VECM), Granger causality, VAR forecasts, impulse responses and variance decomposition, ARIMA forecasts, regressions (OLS, WLS, GLS, quantile, logistic, probit, IV/2SLS, Fama-MacBeth, fixed and random effects panels), causal designs (difference-in-differences, event study, regression discontinuity, synthetic control, propensity score matching), diagnostics (ARCH-LM, Jarque-Bera, Ljung-Box, Durbin-Watson, Breusch-Pagan, White, Ramsey RESET, VIF, Chow, CUSUM, variance ratio) and forecast comparison (Diebold-Mariano, RMSE, MAE). No need to fetch price data first. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers.

tools.name: options
tools.description: Option pricing and Greeks (Black-Scholes model, binomial tree, delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho, implied volatility). Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. get_stock_price_simulation returns the unique price levels per time step; pass show_unique_combinations=false for every simulated path. get_binomial_model covers the strikes within 5% of the price unless strike_price_range= asks for more; strike_price_range also narrows the Greeks and get_option_chains. get_option_chains shows the nearest expiry (its Expiration Date column says which); show_expiration_dates=true lists the expiries and expiration_date= picks one. get_strategy_payoff takes legs as a list of objects, e.g. [{'strike_price': 340, 'position': 'long'}, {'strike_price': 360, 'position': 'short'}].

tools.name: government
tools.description: Government fiscal metrics by country (debt, deficit, expenditure, revenue, tax revenue, trust in government). Requires countries='United States' — use comma-separated values for multiple countries. Do NOT use tickers= for this tool. Supports start_date/end_date. Most series are yearly: quarterly=true returns quarterly data only where a source has it (a note says when it does not). Supports rolling=N (moving-average smoothing) and trailing=N (trailing N-period sum, e.g. a trailing-4-quarter sum) on the raw series. level='consolidated' (default, longest history), 'general' (general government) or 'central' (central government) selects the level of government for debt, deficit, expenditure, revenue and tax revenue.

tools.name: macroeconomics
tools.description: Macroeconomic indicators by country (GDP, real GDP, CPI, PPI, inflation rate, trade balance, imports, exports, investment, consumption, business/consumer confidence, house prices, rent prices, exchange rates, real effective exchange rate, money supply, household savings rate, household debt-to-income ratio, output gap, real interest rate, misery index, banking/currency/sovereign debt crisis indicators, commercial real estate prices, commodity forward curves). Requires countries='United States' — use comma-separated values for multiple countries. Do NOT use tickers= for this tool. Supports start_date/end_date. Indicators with a period come at the highest frequency they are published at unless period= says otherwise (daily, else weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly); the others are yearly. quarterly=true returns quarterly data only where a source has it (a note says when it does not). Supports rolling=N (moving-average smoothing) and trailing=N (trailing N-period sum, e.g. a trailing-4-quarter sum) on the raw series. get_gross_domestic_product_growth returns the latest quarterly real GDP growth (quarter on quarter, or year_over_year=true) without an API key. get_shiller_stock_market_data returns Robert Shiller's monthly US stock market data from 1871 (price, dividend, earnings, CPI, long rate, CAPE; no countries needed). get_exchange_rates defaults to daily rates and accepts end_of_period=true for month-, quarter- or year-end rates (BIS, no key). get_commercial_real_estate_prices covers around twenty economies (BIS, no key). get_inflation_rate and get_consumer_price_index default to monthly data (period='yearly' for annual), without an API key (Eurostat incl. the euro area flash estimate, the ONS for the United Kingdom, the Statistics Bureau of Japan, and the BIS for around sixty other countries incl. the United States, China, India and Brazil). get_consumer_price_index also accepts oecd_source=true for monthly/quarterly OECD data only. get_commodity_forward_curve requires a commodity= argument instead of countries= (e.g. 'Crude Oil', 'Gold') and returns dated futures contracts, not a country series. Also includes six US-only indicators that only return a 'United States' column regardless of the countries= argument: get_industrial_production_index (Federal Reserve G.17) and get_recession_indicator (NBER business cycle dates) work without an API key, while get_retail_sales, get_housing_starts, get_real_personal_income and get_commercial_real_estate_prices require a free FRED API key (optional; get one at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html). get_economic_calendar returns scheduled economic data releases (event, previous, estimate, actual, impact) rather than a country series. By default it returns only High impact releases from the past 23 days to the coming 7 days; narrow it with countries= (e.g. 'United States') and currencies= (e.g. 'USD,EUR'), filter on event names with events= (e.g. events='PMI' for the purchasing managers' indices with consensus, or 'CPI,Unemployment'), pass impact='Medium' or 'High,Medium' for more, impact='All' for every release, and start_date/end_date for another window (keep it to a few weeks: one month of every country is over 2,000 releases). Its Unit column gives each release's unit; releases quoted in percent and its Change % column are decimals like the rest. Every rate and ratio this tool returns is a decimal fraction, not a percentage: an inflation rate of 4.1% comes back as 0.0412 and a debt-to-GDP ratio of 131.7% as 1.3173. Multiply by 100 before presenting them as percentages. Global Macro Database options: usd=true returns GDP, GDP per capita, consumption, investment, fixed investment, exports, imports, trade balance and current account in millions of US dollars (comparable across countries); get_total_consumption and get_total_consumption_to_gdp_ratio accept component='total', 'household' or 'government'; get_house_prices with inflation_adjusted=true returns real house prices. Yearly GMDB series end at the last observation; pass gmdb_forecasts=true to include the IMF projections up to five years ahead. get_implied_volatility returns volatility indices by market and maturity as decimals, no countries needed (markets='US Equity' VIX 9D-1Y from 1990, 'Euro Area Equity' VSTOXX 1M-24M from 1999, 'Emerging Markets Equity', 'US Equity Volatility' VVIX, 'US Treasury Bonds' VXTLT, 'Crude Oil', 'Gold'; with an FMP key also 'US Treasury Rates' MOVE and 'Japan Government Bonds'), period='daily', 'weekly' or 'monthly'. get_stress_test_scenario returns regulators' stress test scenarios (authority='federal_reserve' quarterly US and international variables incl. Treasury and BBB yields, equity, house prices and VIX; authority='esrb' the EBA bank stress test, yearly, every EU country plus iTraxx spreads), scenario='baseline', 'adverse' or 'historic' (Fed history from 1976), countries= optional; the scenario path is not cut to start_date/end_date. Long-horizon data: get_long_run_asset_returns returns yearly total returns 1870-2020 for 18 advanced economies (Jordà-Schularick-Taylor; asset_class='equity'|'housing'|'bonds'|'bills'|'risky'|'safe'|'wealth', real=true for real returns; licensed for non-commercial use only, so it requires accept_licence=true; countries= optional). get_millennium_of_macroeconomic_data returns the Bank of England's annual UK series from as early as 1086 to 2016 (series= e.g. 'Bank Rate,Consols,Share prices'; set start_date far back, e.g. 1700-01-01). get_scenario_set returns De Nederlandsche Bank's pension scenario set (20,000 scenarios over 100 years, measure='real_world' or 'market_consistent'): quantiles per horizon year of nominal zero rates 1Y-30Y, the euro area 10Y real rate, equity returns and EU/NL inflation; the first call takes one to two minutes. get_asset_class_proxies returns monthly total returns of listed funds tracking private equity, infrastructure, hedge funds, merger arbitrage, private credit, real estate and investment grade and high yield credit (asset_classes=, period='daily'|'weekly'|'monthly').

tools.name: environment
tools.description: Environmental and ESG data. For ESG scores (E, S, G ratings) use tickers='AAPL'. For carbon footprint and renewable energy data use countries='United States' (also supports rolling=N and trailing=N smoothing/summation). This is the only tool that accepts BOTH tickers= and countries= depending on the indicator. get_carbon_price returns the EU ETS carbon price (EEX primary auctions of EU emission allowances, euro per tonne of CO2, daily from 2020, no key and no countries needed), period='daily', 'weekly' or 'monthly'. get_climate_scenario returns NGFS climate scenario paths (Phase 5, yearly 2022-2050, around fifty countries and regions, no key): variable='gdp'|'inflation'|'long_term_interest_rate'|'long_term_real_interest_rate'|'policy_rate'|'unemployment_rate'|'equity_prices'|'effective_exchange_rate'|'oil_price'|'gas_price'|'coal_price'|'carbon_price' (carbon price per model region to 2100), scenario='Net Zero 2050'|'Below 2°C'|'Low demand'|'Delayed transition'|'Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)'|'Current Policies'|'Fragmented World'|'Baseline', model='REMIND-MAgPIE'|'GCAM'|'MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM', risk='combined'|'transition'|'physical', deviation=true for the deviation from the baseline; countries= optional.

tools.name: jobs
tools.description: Labour and social metrics by country (unemployment rate, labour productivity, population statistics, poverty rate, income inequality). Requires countries='United States' — use comma-separated values for multiple countries. Do NOT use tickers= for this tool. Supports start_date/end_date. Indicators with a period come at the highest frequency they are published at unless period= says otherwise; the others are yearly. quarterly=true returns quarterly data only where a source has it (a note says when it does not). get_life_table returns Eurostat life tables by age 0-95 for European countries, yearly from 1960 (measure='death_probability'|'survival_probability'|'death_rate'|'survivors'|'deaths'|'person_years'|'total_person_years'|'life_expectancy', sex='total'|'male'|'female'); keep countries to one or two, since each country has 96 ages. get_unemployment_rate defaults to monthly figures without an API key (Eurostat, the ONS for the United Kingdom, the IBGE for Brazil, the BLS for the latest US months, the OECD for every other country). Supports rolling=N (moving-average smoothing) and trailing=N (trailing N-period sum) on the raw series. Also includes two US-only, FRED-backed labor indicators (get_nonfarm_payrolls, get_initial_jobless_claims) — these require a FRED API key and only return a 'United States' column regardless of the countries= argument.

tools.name: rates
tools.description: Interest rate data (central bank policy rates, short/long-term rates, government bond yields, ICE BofA corporate bond series, EURIBOR, ECB rates, Federal Reserve rates, official U.S. Treasury par yield curve, yield curve slope). Requires countries='United States' — use comma-separated values for multiple countries. Do NOT use tickers= for this tool. Supports start_date/end_date. Indicators with a period come at the highest frequency they are published at unless period= says otherwise (daily, else weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly); keep the date range short for daily series. quarterly=true returns quarterly data only where a source has it (a note says when it does not). Without an API key: get_central_bank_policy_rate defaults to daily rates (BIS, around fifty central banks incl. 'Euro Area'); get_long_term_interest_rate defaults to daily 10-year yields for the United States, United Kingdom, Japan and Euro Area and to monthly otherwise; get_overnight_rate returns €STR, SONIA, TONA and SOFR (Euro Area, United Kingdom, Japan, United States) with period='daily', 'weekly' or 'monthly'. get_government_bond_yield_curve returns full government yield curves (columns per country and maturity, e.g. 3M to 30Y) for the United States, Euro Area, Germany, United Kingdom, Japan, Canada, Sweden, Norway and Australia, daily, weekly or monthly, plus the monthly 10-year yield of every other EU member (e.g. France, Italy, Spain) with period='monthly'; keep the date range short (a few weeks) or use period='monthly', since one country is up to 15 maturities per day. get_treasury_rates returns the US par yield curve and works without an API key. Curve analytics without an API key, on the curves of get_government_bond_yield_curve (the full history from start_date, so use period='monthly' for long ranges): get_zero_coupon_curve (zero-coupon rates bootstrapped from the par yields; United States, Euro Area, Germany, Japan, Canada, Sweden; countries= optional, United States by default), get_nelson_siegel_svensson (Svensson parameters Beta 0-3, Tau 1-2 and the fit error per date, svensson=false for the three-factor Nelson-Siegel level/slope/curvature; maturities='0.5,1,10,50' returns the fitted zero-coupon yields instead), get_yield_curve_principal_components (one country: level/slope/curvature loadings with the explained variance as the last row, scores=true for the scores per date, changes=false to analyze levels), get_short_rate_model (one country: Vasicek and CIR calibrated to the history of the short_rate='3M' yield, with the model's zero-coupon curve next to the market's; CIR needs a rate above zero throughout, so use short_rate='6M' or a later start_date for the US) and get_short_rate_simulation (one country: model='hull_white' (fits today's curve), 'vasicek' or 'cir'; short_rate=, years=, steps_per_year=, paths=; returns the mean and 5-95% percentiles per step). get_treasury_auctions returns US Treasury auction results (no countries needed; security_type='Bill'|'Cash Management Bill'|'Note'|'Bond'|'TIPS'|'FRN', security_term= e.g. '10-Year'; yield, bid-to-cover ratio, amounts and primary dealer/direct/indirect bidder shares, from 1979; keep the date range short). The central bank policy rate, short/long-term rate, overnight rate and yield curve slope indicators additionally support rolling=N (moving-average smoothing) and trailing=N (trailing N-period sum). Also includes get_mortgage_rate_30_year (Freddie Mac, US only, works without an API key). Inflation-linked curves without an API key, columns per country and maturity, countries= optional: get_real_yield_curve (real yields of inflation-linked government bonds: United States TIPS, United Kingdom index-linked gilts, Germany inflation-linked federal bonds at constant maturities) and get_breakeven_inflation_expectations (market-implied inflation, nominal minus real: United States incl. 5Y5Y forward, United Kingdom RPI implied inflation, Germany as the euro area proxy), both with period='daily', 'weekly' or 'monthly'; get_inflation_expectations (survey-based longer-term inflation expectations: Germany 5Y and 10Y monthly from 1989 via Consensus Economics, Euro Area 5Y from the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters from 1999), period='monthly' or 'quarterly'. Long-history US credit series: get_hqm_corporate_bond_yield_curve (Treasury HQM corporate curve, rate='spot' for 6 months to 100 years or 'par', monthly from 1984), get_hqm_corporate_bond_spread (HQM par minus Treasury yields at 2, 5, 10 and 30 years, from 1984), get_moodys_corporate_bond_yields (Aaa and Baa, daily from 1986 or period='monthly' from 1919; spread=true for the spreads over the 10-year Treasury and Baa - Aaa) and get_excess_bond_premium (Gilchrist-Zakrajšek credit spread, excess bond premium and implied recession probability, monthly from 1973, no key needed). Also without a key: get_eiopa_risk_free_rate (EIOPA Solvency II risk-free curves for the euro and 40 other currencies, 1 to 150 years, monthly from 2023; countries= e.g. 'Euro Area,United Kingdom', curve='spot_no_va'|'spot_with_va'|'shock_up'|'shock_down'; returns the 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30 year maturities unless maturity_years= lists others, e.g. '1,3,7,50'), get_bank_of_england_yield_curve (UK zero-coupon spot curve, curve='nominal'|'ois', 0.5 to 40 years, daily from 1985), get_corporate_borrowing_cost (ECB cost of bank borrowing for euro area companies, monthly from 2003), get_corporate_bond_yields (monthly corporate bond yields by country: Germany all ratings from 1957 (Bundesbank), Australia A and BBB at 3, 5, 7 and 10 years from 2005 (RBA), United States Moody's Aaa/Baa with a FRED key; spread=true for the spread over government bonds), get_rating_transition_matrix (ESMA CEREP rating migration matrix of a rating agency, agency='S&P'|'Moody's'|'Fitch'|'DBRS'|'Scope'|..., rating_type='corporate'|'sovereign'|'structured_finance'|'covered_bonds', year=, horizon= years, region= e.g. 'Europe'; probabilities, withdrawal-adjusted), get_default_rates (one-year default rates per rating per year from the agency's first reported year, ESMA CEREP; slow the first time, about 30 seconds per year), get_eiopa_symmetric_adjustment (Solvency II equity dampener and type 1/type 2 equity charges, daily from 1991) and get_financial_stress_index (ECB CISS for the euro area, its members, the UK, US and China, daily from 1980). The HQM, Moody's and ICE BofA series require a free FRED API key (get one at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html).

tools.name: fixed_income
tools.description: Bond and derivative valuation calculations (bond duration, present value, yield to maturity, derivative pricing, par yield, forward rate, breakeven inflation rate, key rate duration, yield curve spread, Z-spread, bond-equivalent yield, Taylor-series price change estimate). No tickers or countries needed — pass the bond's terms directly, e.g. par_value=1000, coupon_rate=0.05, years_to_maturity=10 with bond_price or yield_to_maturity. A bond's price is get_present_value. The curve-based calculations (par yield, forward rate, yield curve spread, Z-spread, key rate duration, breakeven inflation) take the curve as spot_rates (nominal_rates and real_rates for breakeven inflation), the rate per maturity in years, e.g. {'1': 0.042, '2': 0.040, '5': 0.041, '10': 0.043}; without it they use a fixed sample curve for illustration. Take the current curve from the rates tool, e.g. get_treasury_rates or get_zero_coupon_curve. get_option_adjusted_spread values a callable bond on a Ho-Lee tree (bond_price, coupon_rate, years_to_maturity, call_price, years_to_first_call, volatility=0.01) and returns the OAS, the straight bond price, the option value and the effective duration and convexity; without spot_rates it uses the current US Treasury zero-coupon curve. get_implied_default_probability turns credit spreads (spreads=0.012 or 'BBB:0.011, B:0.031', recovery_rate=0.4, horizons='1,5,10') into hazard rates and default probabilities; without spreads it uses the latest ICE BofA spread per rating, which needs a FRED API key.

tools.name: discovery
tools.description: Market discovery (lists of stocks, ETFs, indices, currencies, commodities and cryptocurrencies, stock screener, biggest gainers and losers, most active stocks, sector and industry performance and P/E, earnings, IPO and stock split calendars, latest 8-K filings, insider trades and mergers, market news and press releases). No tickers or countries needed. The calendars and filings take start_date/end_date; the market-wide earnings calendar covers the coming week unless a range is given. Sector and industry performance and P/E take date= for one day's snapshot or sector=/industry= for a history (the last year unless start_date/end_date say otherwise). The stock screener ranks by market cap in US dollars ('Market Cap (USD)'; 'Market Cap' is in the listing's own currency) and returns every listing of a company unless primary_only=true; to screen by classification, use the Finance Database server.

tools.name: market_data
tools.description: Raw financial data (historical prices, income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, company profile, quotes, analyst estimates, dividend/earnings calendars, statistics, market risk premium by country, CFTC Commitment of Traders report, executives and their compensation, company notes, employee count, share float, mergers and acquisitions, stock splits, insider trade statistics, analyst stock grades, ETF/fund holdings, information and country/sector weightings, earnings call transcripts). Use this ONLY for raw data needs — for pre-computed ratios, performance, risk, or model metrics use the dedicated tools instead. Requires tickers='AAPL' — use comma-separated values for multiple tickers. get_market_risk_premium (by country) and get_treasury_data (US Treasury rates) are market-wide and need no tickers. get_commitment_of_traders takes CFTC futures symbols, e.g. tickers='NG' (natural gas) or 'GC' (gold), not stocks. The ETF/fund methods return no data for tickers that are not an ETF or fund. get_earnings_call_transcripts returns the full, never shortened text (often 40,000 to 60,000 characters) of one call of one ticker: the most recent, or the one of fiscal_period (e.g. '2025Q4', the company's own fiscal quarter); call it once per ticker and period. A period without a transcript is answered with the most recent periods that have one. Currency and crypto pairs may be written either way: EURUSD or EURUSD=X, BTCUSD or BTC-USD. To find which instruments exist, use the Finance Database server. get_etf_holdings returns the 25 largest holdings of each fund by weight unless limit= asks for more; it holds no sector or country per holding, so use get_etf_sector_weightings and get_etf_country_weightings for those breakdowns, or the Finance Database server to classify the holdings.

tools.name: search_metric_categories
tools.description: List all available metric categories with tool counts and descriptions.

tools.name: search_by_category
tools.description: List all metrics within a specific category by name.

tools.name: search_metrics
tools.description: Fuzzy keyword search across all 500+ available methods.
